challenges.title: OWTA, Banded Hours and the question of data sovereignty

items.title: Keeping the OWTA weekly working-time limit under control
items.text: The Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 caps average working time at 48 hours a week, with a standard reference period of 4 months. An extension to 6 months applies only to specific activities such as security or healthcare — tracking this by hand is error-prone.

items.title: Banded Hours & shift notice
items.text: Under Section 18A OWTA, employees can apply for placement in a band of hours if their contracted hours don't reflect reality; the employer then has 4 weeks to respond. Section 17 OWTA also requires at least 24 hours' advance notice of start and finish times where the roster isn't fixed.

items.title: Data sovereignty instead of a third-country cloud
items.text: The Data Protection Act 2018 implements the GDPR in Ireland, with the Data Protection Commission (DPC) as the supervisory authority. Especially when it comes to AI features, many businesses have to ask whether staff data may go into a third-country cloud at all.

rulesCalendar.title: Uniform nationwide, split at the border
rulesCalendar.text: The Republic of Ireland has no public holidays at county or municipal level: all statutory holidays apply uniformly nationwide under the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997. For businesses with ties to Northern Ireland, though, what applies across the border still matters — a completely separate holiday regime is in force there.

items.title: No patchwork within Ireland itself
items.text: Unlike many other countries, the Republic of Ireland has no public holidays at county or municipal level — the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 sets all statutory holidays uniformly nationwide. Northern Ireland, as part of the United Kingdom, has an entirely separate regime.

items.title: Combining the Republic and Northern Ireland
items.text: A business in the border region — say, in Dundalk (County Louth) or Letterkenny (County Donegal) — or with locations in Dublin and Belfast keeps both calendars side by side: St. Brigid's Day (the first Monday in February) and the June bank holiday in the Republic, Orangemen's Day (12 July) in Northern Ireland.

items.title: Active or informational only
items.text: You decide per calendar whether a holiday affects hours & surcharges — or simply appears as a reminder.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off Irish businesses
solutions.subtitle: From automatic rest-period checks to your own infrastructure — it all fits together.

items.title: Weekly working-time limit monitored automatically
items.text: Klacks calculates the 48-hour average limit over the reference period set out in OWTA Section 15 — including the sector-specific extension to 6 months for security and healthcare.

items.title: Rest periods observed automatically
items.text: The daily rest period of at least 11 consecutive hours (Section 11) and the weekly rest period of at least 24 hours (Section 13) are monitored in real time — breaches simply never occur.

items.title: Shift notice with 24 hours' lead time
items.text: Klacks makes sure start and finish times are set at least 24 hours in advance whenever the roster isn't fixed, as required by Section 17 OWTA.

items.title: Banded Hours applications documented
items.text: Klacks records actual hours worked over 12 months, so an application for Banded Hours under Section 18A OWTA can be answered cleanly within the 4-week deadline.

items.title: On-premise: full data sovereignty
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure, and you choose the AI model — including locally hosted, with no staff data ever transferred abroad.

items.title: Klacksy: rule-based, not a black box
items.text: The built-in AI assistant Klacksy schedules by voice command — transparently, based on defined skills and rules, not as an opaque AI decision.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the assistant built into your team's workflow
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn't a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it's embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shift times via chat, request shift swaps, or clarify availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy only ever makes transparent suggestions — never a black-box decision. For businesses with strict data protection requirements, the AI model can also be hosted locally, which matters with the DPC in mind too.

example.title: 24 hours' notice, one view
example.text: A schedule changes at short notice. Klacks makes sure the new shift is announced at least 24 hours in advance, as required by Section 17 OWTA, while keeping the 11-hour rest period in view — no manual recalculating required.
